proofs.proof_tex:
Suppose first that every \(\mathcal J_k\) is a singleton.  By the definitions of \(M\) and \(K_0\),
\[
M=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}|\mathcal J_k|
  =\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}1
  =|\mathcal K|=K_0.
\]
There is then one row of \(A\) for each \(k\), and that row has a one in the column indexed by \(k\) and zeros elsewhere.  After matching the fixed row order to the target order, \(A=I_{K_0}\) (and in an arbitrary fixed order it is merely a permutation matrix).  Hence \(\ker(A')=\{0\}\), so the prescribed orthonormal basis \(N\) has zero columns.  Moreover, \(A'b=\omega\) has exactly one solution.  Thus there is no comparison-contrast direction over which either the conditional or constant loading program can optimize.  Proposition \(\ref{prop:two-period-eif-reduction}\) gives the claimed source-transcribed comparison for the two-period, one-target instance of this just-identified case.

Now suppose that \(X\) is degenerate.  Conditioning on \(X\) is then conditioning on the trivial sigma-field.  Since \(\Psi_P\in L_2^0(P)^M\), the definitions of \(\Gamma\) and \(\Omega\) imply
\[
\Gamma(X)
=\operatorname{Cov}_P(\Psi_P\mid X)
=\operatorname{Cov}_P(\Psi_P)
=E_P[\Psi_P\Psi_P']
=\Omega
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\tag{K1}
\]
Consequently the pointwise conditional program and the constant program minimize the same quadratic form over the same affine set.

It remains to verify that their singular-case selectors agree.  Because \(A\) has full column rank, \(b^0=A(A'A)^{-1}\omega\) is feasible, and every feasible vector has a unique representation
\[
b=b^0+Nz,
\qquad z\in\mathbb R^{M-K_0}.
\tag{K2}
\]
Indeed, feasibility gives \(A'(b-b^0)=0\), and the columns of \(N\) are an orthonormal basis of \(\ker(A')\).  Put \(d=N'\Gamma b^0\) and \(H=N'\Gamma N\).  Expanding the common objective in (K2) yields
\[
(b^0+Nz)'\Gamma(b^0+Nz)
=(b^0)'\Gamma b^0+2z'd+z'Hz.
\tag{K3}
\]
The matrix \(H\) is symmetric positive semidefinite.  Lemma \(\ref{lem:singular-operator}\) proves, rather than assumes, that \(d\in\operatorname{range}H\).  Therefore the minimizers of (K3) are exactly the solutions of \(Hz=-d\), namely
\[
z=-H^\dagger d+v,
\qquad v\in\ker H.
\tag{K4}
\]
To see sufficiency directly, if \(Hz=-d\), then for every increment \(u\), the change in (K3) is \(u'Hu\ge0\); necessity follows from the first-order equation for this differentiable convex quadratic.  Since \(H\) is symmetric,
\(\operatorname{range}H=(\ker H)^\perp\), and hence \(-H^\dagger d\perp v\) in (K4).  Also \(b^0\in\operatorname{col}A\), whereas \(Nv\) and \(NH^\dagger d\) lie in \(\ker(A')=(\operatorname{col}A)^\perp\).  Orthonormality of the columns of \(N\) now gives
\[
\|b^0-NH^\dagger d+Nv\|_2^2
=\|b^0\|_2^2+\|H^\dagger d\|_2^2+\|v\|_2^2.
\tag{K5}
\]
Thus the unique minimum-Euclidean-norm member of the quadratic-program argmin is obtained with \(v=0\).  Lemma \(\ref{lem:singular-operator}\) identifies this vector as
\[
b^\star=b^0-NH^\dagger N'\Gamma b^0,
\]
while the equivalent characterization in the definition of \(b^{\mathrm{const}}\) identifies the same vector as \(b^{\mathrm{const}}\).  Together with (K1), this proves \(b^\star=b^{\mathrm{const}}\) under degenerate \(X\), including singular fixed-rank cases.

Finally, the only equality asserted here with an externally published efficient influence function is the exact two-period equality proved in Proposition \(\ref{prop:two-period-eif-reduction}\) from its theorem-level cited leaves.  Its status as the canonical gradient of the present observed-law model follows from the tangent-exhaustion and projection result in Theorem \(\ref{thm:complete-normal-canonical-gradient}\), not from formal resemblance.  The same proposition expressly makes no nesting claim for the distinct staggered-DiD tangent system.  This establishes the final qualification in the theorem.
